readings.source_reading: √c.⟦2?⟧³76ᵇ — a small 3 above a first digit crossed by a diagonal stroke; the struck digit looks like 2
readings.evidence: Native tile [0,0]: at x≈700–780, y≈1570–1620, a 3 sits above the first digit, and that digit carries a slash. The underlying digit is most like 2 but is not secure. On the facing fol. 130b, the pencil entry reads '√c.375(5). Do, Do., ...[by Vaṃśadhara], ... n.d:10:11/13:Beng.'. A pencil ⟷ (x≈390–550, y≈1620–1660) lies just right of the gutter on the target canvas. A pencil 'L' sits left of the gutter (x≈270–300), on the fol. 130b side, with a short line running toward the gutter. The number 375 on fol. 130b does not decide between 276 and 376.

The native tile shows 'yā' with a macron and then 'tra' with no visible macron before 'vidhi'. The struck word has a descender at its start and a 'g…ge' shape, consistent with 'pilgrimage', but the strike-through obscures the letters.

The note is in the shelfmark column at y≈3950–4030. That is the line of d.602(6)'s continuation ('3rd vibhāga…'), directly under d.602(6) at y≈3880. f.59 begins about 130px lower, at y≈4125, after an empty interval. Its position favours d.602(6). Attachment to the ditto f.59 cannot be fully excluded.

The date reads '180' plus a final digit like 6, followed by a mark that may be an altered colon or a query. No clear colon separates it from 17. The scribe word begins with an S-like capital and ends in 'b' with possibly a trailing stroke, so 'Scrib' or 'Scribe' is possible.
